title: Optimize Toolkit Kickstart: primer screens, microcopy, and adaptive screenshot variants for batching/caching & quant UI
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a compact, persona-aware kickoff primer for the Optimize toolkit that bundles progressive onboarding screens, production-ready screenshots, and microcopy for batching, caching, and quantization UI. Deliverables include 8 final screenshots (light + dark variants), export spec, example microcopy strings for tooltips and CTAs, and a QA checklist for engineers and docs writers.
acceptance_criteria: 8 annotated screenshots (4 light, 4 dark) exported at 2x retina with naming convention optimizer_kickstart_<variant>_<mode>.png
Microcopy set (tooltips, banner copy, confirm dialogs) reviewed and approved by PM and DevRel
Figma file with components and tokens shared + locked frames for engineers
Accessibility pass: color contrast >= 4.5:1 for primary CTAs and tooltips checked
Design handoff doc and production checklist posted to Confluence with asset links and GitHub PR reference
design_notes: Persona split: ML Engineer (throughput-first), Platform Engineer (SLO-first), Product Developer (cost-aware)
Progressive reveal pattern: show recommended config, explain the trade-off in 1-2 lines, provide a single CTA: 'Apply & Simulate'
Use compact data cards showing: expected tokens/sec, median latency, estimated cost delta vs baseline
Quantization control UI: slider with three presets (Safe, Balanced, Aggressive) and per-preset explainer tooltip
Batching knob: numeric with suggested ranges and a 'test with sample prompt' inline button
KV caching: toggle with 'preview hit-rate' micrograph and inline suggestion 'enable for repeated prefixes'
Include small animated GIFs (max 1.5s, looping) for demo-only assets to show 'apply & simulated run' — engineering can replace with static if needed for release
decisions: Default onboarding flow will recommend 'Balanced' quant preset and batch size of 8 for anonymous/new users to minimize latency regressions
Expose advanced slider only after user clicks 'Advanced settings' to reduce cognitive load
Dashboard cards will use compact bar + sparkline to indicate recent variance rather than full charts to keep screenshots legible
Dark-mode variants required for marketing and docs; maintain identical layout but adjust token card contrasts
tasks: Finalize microcopy and translate core strings for docs team
Create Figma frames: 1440x900 (desktop), 1280x720 (tablet), 390x844 (mobile preview) — but prioritize desktop exports
Export static PNGs (2x) and light GIF placeholders for demo
Run accessibility contrast check and patch colors if needed
Produce handoff Confluence page with usage guidance and links to Figma + drive assets
Coordinate with engineering to include sample payloads for 'simulate' runs in the QA checklist
